headline: Invention brings new things into existence—transforming imagination into reality
universal_truth: The future is made by those who build it; possibility precedes reality
fun_facts: The wheel wasn't invented until about 3500 BCE—millions of years after humans existed
Many inventions were discovered simultaneously by different inventors unaware of each other
Most patents are never commercialized—invention is just the first step
discussion_questions: What's the difference between invention and innovation?
Why do some inventions succeed while others fail?
What doesn't exist yet that you wish someone would invent?

hook.script: Everything humans have built—every tool, machine, technology—once didn't exist. Someone imagined it, then made it real. Invention is the strange alchemy of transforming what could be into what is. Making something from nothing but ideas.

cliff.script: Inventions seem to appear suddenly—eureka moments and lone geniuses. But is that how new things actually come into existence?

options.text: Most inventions are gradual—built on previous work, responding to needs, and often developed by multiple people simultaneously
options.response: Yes. Inventions rarely spring from nothing. They combine existing elements in new ways, solve recognized problems, and often emerge when the necessary pieces finally exist together.

options.text: Inventions come from creative individuals with unique insights
options.response: Individual creativity matters, but inventions require context and building blocks...

fact1.title: Adjacent Possible
fact1.script: Inventions happen when they become possible—when prerequisite technologies and knowledge exist. The iPhone couldn't happen in 1990; required technologies weren't ready. Inventors work at the edge of what's possible, pushing into what just became achievable.

fact2.title: Simultaneous Discovery
fact2.script: Major inventions are often made simultaneously by separate inventors: telephone, calculus, radio, evolution theory. This suggests inventions aren't random genius—they're inevitable once conditions are right. Ideas whose time has come.

fact3.title: Problem-Driven
fact3.script: Most inventions solve problems. Necessity really is the mother of invention. But seeing the problem clearly is the hard part—many inventions seem obvious in retrospect but required someone to recognize an unmet need.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The future is made by those who build it. Invention teaches that possibility precedes reality—what doesn't exist yet can exist if someone creates it.

outro.script: That's Day 169. Tomorrow, we'll explore finding what was already there—discovery. Until then, consider what problem you might solve by building something new.

growTrack.title: Invention Thinking - What Could Exist?
growTrack.activity: Notice a problem or frustration in your day. What would solve it? Describe your ideal solution without worrying if it's possible. This is how inventors think—starting from the problem, imagining what doesn't exist yet, then working backward to build it.
